Timeline::epoch_millis¶

Back to Timeline API Reference

Signature¶

Series Timeline::epoch_millis() const

Project Instants Onto Millisecond Ticks¶

epoch_millis() counts whole milliseconds from the UTC Unix epoch in a shape-preserving Int64 Series. The operation floors toward negative infinity, which keeps the interval represented by each integer consistent on both sides of the epoch.

const auto times = pluss::timeline::from_epoch(
    {{-1LL, 0LL}, {1'999'999'999LL, pluss::Timeline::kNaT}});
std::cout << pluss::series::print(times.epoch_millis()) << '\n';

Output¶

Series(shape=[2,2], strides=[2,1], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data=
⎡    -1                    0 ⎤
⎣  1999 -9223372036854775808 ⎦

The result is independent of tz(): a timezone changes civil presentation, not distance from the epoch. Nanosecond precision below a millisecond is lost, and NaT is preserved as Timeline::kNaT.
